question: Magnetic lines move from west to east direction and the conductor placed horizontally moves towards the upward direction. In such a case, the direction of induced current is towards:
solution:
The correct answer is** 'north'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Maxwell’s right hand thumb** rule states that, when the current flows from **east to west** direction, the magnetic field will move in a **clockwis**e direction, that is, from the direction **north to south**. Similarly, when the current flows from **west to east **direction, the magnetic field will move in an** anti-clockwise **direction, that is, from the direction **south to north.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Right hand thumb rule** states that whenever there is a conductor and current is flowing in that conductor, then assume as if you are holding the **conductor **in your **right hand with thumb **pointing in the direction of current. With such an orientation of right hand , **curl of fingers** will give** direction of magnetic field.**
